variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Reasoning evaluation tests whether an AI system can use stated evidence, rules, quantities, or constraints to reach a warranted conclusion. It is broader than checking whether an answer string matches: the evaluator must define the capability, select representative items, control the inference protocol, choose a valid scorer, and report uncertainty.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Separate four kinds of reasoning evidence”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Outcome
pairs.detail: Score the final answer against an exact target, executable check, formal verifier, or expert rubric.
pairs.explanation: Score the final answer against an exact target, executable check, formal verifier, or expert rubric. Record abstentions, invalid formats, and tool failures instead of silently dropping them.

pairs.label: Process evidence
pairs.detail: Verify equations, code execution, cited evidence, state transitions, or constraint satisfaction when the domain permits.
pairs.explanation: Verify equations, code execution, cited evidence, state transitions, or constraint satisfaction when the domain permits. Do not reward a rationale merely for being long or plausible.

pairs.label: Robustness
pairs.detail: Pair original items with meaning-preserving and meaning-changing variants.
pairs.explanation: Pair original items with meaning-preserving and meaning-changing variants. Measure unexpected flips, invalid invariance, and sensitivity to prompt or tool settings.

pairs.label: System cost
pairs.detail: Report attempts, tokens, latency, tool calls, failures, and monetary cost under the same protocol.
pairs.explanation: Report attempts, tokens, latency, tool calls, failures, and monetary cost under the same protocol. More test-time work can change both capability and deployability.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. A fluent explanation is useful evidence only when its claims can be checked.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Outcome: Score the final answer against an exact target, executable check, formal verifier, or expert rubric. Process evidence: Verify equations, code execution, cited evidence, state transitions, or constraint satisfaction when the domain permits. Robustness: Pair original items with meaning-preserving and meaning-changing variants. System cost: Report attempts, tokens, latency, tool calls, failures, and monetary cost under the same protocol.

variants.prompt: Which statement is a directly measurable criterion rather than a broad reasoning construct?
options: The system can reason mathematically
The system answers protected multi-step arithmetic items correctly under protocol version 3
The system is generally intelligent
The system understands causality
variants.explanation: A criterion names observable tasks and conditions. Broad constructs such as mathematical reasoning need criteria and evidence before they can be measured.
